facts.why: Kane says 'If the headline is big enough, it makes the news big enough' to Carter in the office on his first day, over the Silverstone story, not at the party for the Chronicle men six years later.
facts.fix: to Carter, on his first day

facts.why: Badge reads 'NEW YORK INQUIRER / Drama critic: J. Leland / Fired by Kane'. Leland asks to be transferred to the Chicago paper as its drama critic, and he is fired after his review of Susan's Chicago opera debut, so he was on the Chicago Inquirer.
facts.full: NEW YORK INQUIRER / Drama critic: J. Leland / Fired by Kane

facts.text: ON THE BEAT. Another frame from Citizen Kane.
facts.why: Stock layout caption. The still above it is the snow globe, which falls from Kane's hand as he says 'Rosebud'. The caption says nothing about it.
facts.fix: ROSEBUD. The snow globe falls from Kane's hand.

notes: Writer's doubt settled: the welcome is a celebration party in the Inquirer city room at a long table laid with champagne, a K ice sculpture and ice busts of Leland and Bernstein (Filmsite), so 'Inquirer Welcome Dinner' and the champagne line are fair. 684,132 confirmed (Bernstein). 'You still eating?' 'I'm still hungry.', the peanuts line, love nest with quote singer unquote, forty-nine thousand acres, 'Another Venus' and the crated statue all on Wikiquote. 'No. 1941' and 'Now showing, 1941' match the story's present (Kane dies in 1941).

vibe.verdict: A real Inquirer front page with Rosebud, Leland's review and Xanadu's crates, but the food is generic period dining and two of the best scenes are missing.
missing: Emily's breakfast table montage: 'Really Charles, people will think...' 'What I tell them to think.'
Thatcher reads 'I think it would be fun to run a newspaper.'
The sled burning in the furnace (ending)
'Are we going to declare war on Spain, or are we not?' 'The Inquirer already has.' (the party)
